sovereign_country.strategic_role: 泛欧数字贸易门户、极速低成本在线设立与新锐EMI银行开户

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

meta_jurisdiction_context.sovereign_country_en: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Gibraltar (British Overseas Territory of the United Kingdom)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law of England and Wales as the residuary substratum, with a substantial Gibraltar statutory overlay; corporate origin in the Bermuda Exempted Company governed by the Common Law-based Bermuda Companies Act 1981)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Bermuda Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1986, as amended by the 2004 and 2006 Protocols)
OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (extended to Gibraltar and Bermuda)
UK-Gibraltar Economic Substance Arrangement concluded at the EU Code of Conduct Group (2019)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary instruments: (i) Gibraltar Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the Proceeds of Crime (Amendment) Act 2021; (ii) Gibraltar Sanctions Act 2020 and the Sanctions Regulations 2020; (iii) Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 174), as amended, together with the Companies (Register of Beneficial Owners) Rules 2019; (iv) Economic Substance (Company and Limited Partnership) Act 2019; (v) Gibraltar Financial Services Commission AML/CFT Guidance Notes (current edition); and, at the place of incorporation, (vi) Bermuda Companies Act 1981 as amended, Bermuda Proceeds of Crime Act 1997, the Proceeds of Crime (Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing) Regulations 2020 (Bermuda), and the Bermuda Beneficial Ownership (Companies) Regulations 2018.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Bermuda Exempted Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bermuda Registrar of Companies, Government of Bermuda

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (restated and notarially certified)
Certificate of Good Standing issued for the purpose of Gibraltar registration or continuation
Resolution of Incorporator and Schedule of Beneficial Ownership (UBO declaration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator and licensed Bermuda corporate services provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Registration as a Foreign (Oversea) Company or Certificate of Continuation issued by the Gibraltar Companies Registry
Registered Office Consent and Letter of Undertaking from the Gibraltar licensed corporate services provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Bermuda Companies Act 1981 (as amended), Sections 4, 5, 13, 14, 18 and 20 (Exempted Company provisions); registered in Gibraltar pursuant to the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014, Part X (Overseas Companies) and the Beneficial Ownership (Secure Search) Regulations 2017.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (incorporation) and Gibraltar Companies House (foreign company registration and beneficial ownership filing)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association (Exempted Company Form) together with Form M1 (Notice of Exempted Company) for Bermuda and Form OSC-1 (Overseas Company Registration) for Gibraltar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. A single subscriber share of US$0.01 is issued. No escrow account or capital deposit is required for this non-regulated e-commerce retail activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) the subscribers' acquisition of 1,000 fully paid ordinary shares of US$0.01 each is approved; (2) the Registered Office of the Company shall be established at [Address], Gibraltar, with the licensed registered agent; (3) [Director] and [Director] are appointed as authorised directors, and [Secretary] as Corporate Secretary; (4) the board is empowered to file all incorporation forms and constitutional documents, to open merchant and EMI bank accounts, and to instruct counsel regarding exempt status and licensing matters; (5) any one director may certify and execute all necessary instruments and statutory returns for implementation. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the statutory registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Exempted Company Name Clearance and Status Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Bermuda Registrar of Companies (via licensed corporate service provider in Gibraltar)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name and a declaration of exempted status through the jurisdiction's online forming agent. The registrar conducts a conflict search and approves the name subject to deceptiveness screening. For fast-fashion e-commerce, a clean name (e.g., 'Fast Fashion Digital Limited') is usually approved within one working day.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of subscribers and directors
Proof of residential address for each officer (utility bill)
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused due to similarity or obscenity, resubmit two alternates under the same submission code within 24 hours; no additional fee is charged if the resubmission is made on the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar-licensed notary public and UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (apostille)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Executed pages of the Memorandum and Articles of Association are notarised by a Gibraltar notary. Where required, the notary's certificate is apostilled by the UK FCDO for presentation to the Bermuda Registry. The same set of documents is subsequently used for the Gibraltar branch registration.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act as director and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies an execution defect, cure by a directors' supplemental declaration and re-notarisation within 48 hours; the notary fee is waived for the correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Filing with the Bermuda Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The corporate service provider files the Form M1 (Notice of Exempted Company), constitution documents, subscriber consents, and the statutory filing fee online. The Registrar reviews the submission and issues a Certificate of Incorporation after a manual check. For standard e-commerce holding companies, issuance occurs within three working days.
required_dossiers: Notarised and apostilled Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered office address confirmation in Bermuda
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a requisition, address the requested amendment within seven official working days and pay a re-filing fee of US$100; expedited handling is available for an additional US$150.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Gibraltar Foreign Company Registration and Beneficial Ownership Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Bermuda Exempted Company as a foreign company under the Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 using Form OSC-1. File beneficial ownership particulars to the Gibraltar Beneficial Ownership Secure Search (BOSS) system. Establish a registered office address in Gibraltar through the licensed agent.
required_dossiers: Notarised board resolution to register as a foreign company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar rejects the filing for incomplete beneficial ownership details, rectify by submitting a confirmation statement within five business days, quoting the original submission ID; no re-filing fee applies if accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax-Exempt Status and E-Commerce Licensing Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Income Tax Office and Gibraltar Business Licensing Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for confirmation of non-resident/exempt status under the Gibraltar Income Tax Act exemption provisions applicable to foreign-incorporated companies. Simultaneously verify that no business license is required for ISIC 4791 (online apparel retail). If payment service providers require regulatory comfort, obtain a letter of no-licence from the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission.
required_dossiers: Business plan describing the e-commerce activity
Declaration confirming no physical production facilities in Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office queries economic substance, file a detailed explanation of core income-generating activities (online sales) and submit the revised exempt company return within 30 days. Any licensing refusal may be appealed to the Registration and Appeals Tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Gibraltar Business Licensing Authority (GBLA) — no permit required for online retail
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating licence required; standard business registration certificate from Gibraltar Companies House

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Heritage and Climate Change (Gibraltar)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt — online-only activity with no industrial installation; no EIA required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC emissions. For the leased office, applicable standards are the Gibraltar Code for Engineering Works and municipal waste segregation rules. HVAC systems must comply with the Energy Performance of Buildings Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Gibraltar Fire & Rescue Service, means-of-escape inspection, electrical installation certificate, and occupational health and safety registration as a low-risk office workplace.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Her Majesty's Commissioner of Income Tax, Income Tax Office, HM Government of Gibraltar (8 Secretary's Lane, Gibraltar GX11 1AA); foreign-company registration is administered by the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014; official portal: https://www.gibraltar.gov.gi (Income Tax Office and e-filing sections). Gibraltar is a British Overseas Territory with fiscal autonomy and is not part of the UK for VAT or direct-tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Establish nexus: The Bermuda Exempted Company (Bermuda Exempted Co) must register as an overseas company with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under Part 20 of the Companies Act 2014 within one month of setting up a place of business, branch, or tax-relevant physical presence in Gibraltar; alternatively a full continuation of domicile into Gibraltar may be effected under the Companies (Transfer of Domicile) Act 2004. Step 2 - Lodgment: File certified copies of the Bermuda certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, certificate of good standing from the Bermuda Registrar, register/registered office address in Gibraltar, and particulars of directors and company secretary. Step 3 - Tax registration: Submit the completed corporate taxpayer application to the Income Tax Office; the Commissioner of Income Tax assigns the Gibraltar Tax Identification Number (TIN/tax reference) to the company, normally within 5-10 business days of receipt of the complete file. Step 4 - Compliance cycle: The company becomes chargeable under the Income Tax Act 2010 on Gibraltar-source profits (and on worldwide profits if managed and controlled in Gibraltar, i.e. tax-resident); an annual corporation tax return is due within 12 months of the accounting-period end (31 December basis as standard). Step 5 - Nil-return duty: A dormant or loss-making entity must still file nil/declaration returns; the Bermuda Tax Exemption Certificate does NOT relieve Gibraltar-taxable profits of the Gibraltar permanent establishment, although no capital gains tax, withholding tax, or wealth tax applies in Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (Bermuda domestic status: the Exempted Co holds an irrevocable Tax Exemption Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966, guaranteeing freedom from Bermuda income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax until at least 2035, with Government commitment to periodic extension). The Gibraltar permanent establishment or tax-resident branch is nevertheless subject to Entity_Level_Taxation under Gibraltar law at the flat corporation tax rate of 10% (a 12.5% rate applied only to profits above GBP 500,000 between 2015 and 2020; the top-up was phased out). Territorial_Scope: non-resident companies are taxed only on Gibraltar-source income; pass-through treatment is not available to corporate entities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Bermuda: (i) application for Tax Exemption Certificate under the Exempted Undertakings Tax Protection Act 1966; (ii) designation as a 'long-term undertaking' extending statutory protection to 2050/2060; (iii) election as a permitted entity under the Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2018 for the relevant activity. Gibraltar: no US-style check-the-box election exists; classification is fixed by the Companies Act 2014 legal form. Available Gibraltar elections: (i) group-loss relief surrender election for 75% related persons (Income Tax Act 2010, s.132); (ii) participation exemption/rollover treatment on disposal of qualifying shareholdings (s.126); (iii) capital-allowances pooling and apportionment elections. Hybrid mismatch rules: Gibraltar transposed OECD BEPS Action 2 via the Taxation (Hybrid and Other Mismatches) Regulations effective 1 January 2022; the rules impose mandatory deduction-denials for hybrid financial instruments, hybrid entities, and reverse hybrids (including UK/EU branch mismatches) and contain no elective mitigation, aligning with the UK's and EU ATAD's anti-hybrid frameworks.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Gibraltar has NO value-added tax, NO GST and NO general sales tax; Gibraltar is expressly excluded from the EU VAT system and EU Customs Union (Treaty of Accession 1972, Art. 28 and Annex I, Part I) and remains outside the UK VAT territory. Fiscal excise/customs duties apply only to a closed list of imported goods (alcohol, tobacco, hydrocarbon oils, and motor vehicles). Extraterritorial nexus: the fast-fashion e-commerce operator becomes subject to UK VAT (Value Added Tax Act 1994) on distance sales into the UK and to EU VAT (Directive 2006/112/EC) on consumer supplies into EU Member States, via the OSS and IOSS digital regimes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Gibraltar: no indirect-tax registration threshold (no VAT). UK VAT: GBP 90,000 annual taxable turnover (from 1 April 2024) for distance sales of goods to UK consumers; online marketplaces that facilitate supplies of imported goods valued at up to GBP 135 are deemed suppliers and must register irrespective of threshold. EU VAT: EUR 10,000 annual cross-border distance-sale threshold for intra-EU B2C supplies (Art. 59c of VAT Directive); EUR 150 per-consignment threshold for Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) eligibility, above which import VAT applies at the destination Member State rate; no threshold applies to Union OSS/Non-Union OSS registration once any taxable distance or domestic EU supply is made.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Gibraltar: no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory e-invoicing, no API-based government clearance, and no digital stamping regime; accounting records and underlying e-commerce transaction logs must be retained for 7 years (Income Tax Act 2010, s.154; Companies Act 2014, Part 26). Where the Bermudan Exempted Co is registered for UK VAT, Making Tax Digital (MTD) requires digital-record keeping and quarterly filing through functional compatible software (VATA 1994 Sch. 11; SI 2018/261). Where registered for EU OSS/IOSS: OSS returns are filed quarterly and IOSS returns monthly via the registration Member State's web portal; certain destination Member States impose domestic B2B e-invoicing mandates (e.g., Italy SDI/FatturaPA, France e-invoicing from 2026 under ViDA transposition) only where the company holds local B2B VAT registrations. No e-invoice mandate applies to B2C fast-fashion garment sales settled through the target payment rails (Klarna BNPL, Shopify Payments).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable as a Gibraltar domestic concept because Gibraltar imposes no VAT; goods exported from Gibraltar are outside any Gibraltar indirect-tax charge and there is no Gibraltar zero-rating claim or VAT-refund mechanism. Where the Bermuda Exempted Co voluntarily registers for UK VAT as a non-established taxable person, export supplies of goods from Great Britain to non-UK destinations qualify for the 0% rate under VATA 1994, s.30 and SI 1995/2518, Reg. 129, provided the goods are exported within 3 months of the time of supply and the supplier holds valid commercial evidence of export (customs declaration plus transport documents). For EU consumer sales, goods imported into the EU with a consignment value of EUR 150 or less qualify for exemption from import VAT under the IOSS procedure, with output VAT declared at the destination Member State's standard rate at point of sale; intra-EU distance sales above the EUR 10,000 threshold are declared under OSS. Offshore services (e.g., digital marketing), if exported to non-resident business customers, may be zero-rated under UK VAT place-of-supply B2B rules (reverse charge applies to the recipient).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration: GB Customs Declaration Service (CDS) electronic export declaration (SAD format, C88) with confirmed exit status showing the exporter of record, commodity code (ISIC 4791 / HS Chapters 61-62 apparel), value, and final destination; or, if consigned from an EU Member State, the EU MRN from the National Export System with ECS exit confirmation.

Bill of Lading / Master or House Air Waybill / CMR international consignment note issued by the contracted carrier, evidencing physical removal of the goods from the UK/EU territory and signed receipt by the foreign consignee (this document is the primary evidence of export under UK Customs Notice 703 and EU Reg. 282/2011, Art. 14).

Inward Remittance Certificate: bank SWIFT MT103/credit advice (the internationally accepted equivalent of an inward remittance certificate) confirming receipt of the export sale proceeds by the Bermuda/Gibraltar bank account of the seller, matching the invoiced value, within 180 days of shipment.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: UK VAT: if a zero-rated export is later disproved (goods never exported, diverted, or re-imported into the UK/EU), HMRC raises an assessment for the output tax plus default interest under VATA 1994 s.74 and behavior-based penalties of up to 100% of the tax (Schedule 24, Finance Act 2007); fraudulent claims or false documents trigger criminal prosecution under VATA 1994 s.72 (up to 7 years' imprisonment and unlimited fine) and forfeiture of goods under CEMA 1979 s.167. EU: Art. 14 of Implementing Regulation 282/2011 mandates retrospective correction of the VAT exemption where goods are altered or re-imported into the Union; Member States may assess unpaid VAT for 3-10 years (unlimited in the case of fraud for many States), with default interest and penalties (e.g., Germany AO s.370 up to 10 years' imprisonment; France CGI Art. 1741 up to EUR 500,000 and 5 years). Gibraltar: the Income Tax Office may raise assessments up to 6 years from the end of the accounting period (no time limit for fraud or wilful default), with late-filing daily penalties and civil penalties up to 200% of the tax understated for deliberate inaccuracies (Income Tax Act 2010, s.155); criminal prosecution may additionally apply for false statements. A successful clawback will also disqualify subsequent zero-rating claims and increase the entity's tax-risk rating for EMI and acquirer banking reviews.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Composite authority structure: the Government of Gibraltar (under the Currency Notes Act 1934) is the issuing authority for the Gibraltar pound (GIP), pegged at par to GBP; the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC) is the integrated regulator for banking conduct, AML/CFT supervision, and clearing oversight; the Bank of England remains relevant for sterling monetary policy and CHAPS/Faster Payments infrastructure. There is no autonomous Gibraltar central bank and no separate foreign-exchange control authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bermuda Exempted Company Annual Return (Companies Act 1981 s.174)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation or within 30 days after the annual general meeting if AGM is not dispensed with
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 200 per month or part thereof; failure to pay for 3 consecutive months triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Economic Substance Unit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of the financial year end, e.g., 30 April for a calendar year-end company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to USD 100,000 plus daily default penalty of USD 500; repeated default may lead to administrative strike-off and referral for prosecution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Bermuda (Beneficial Ownership Register)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of incorporation, plus a 30-day grace period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Initial penalty of USD 5,000 and daily default fine of USD 500; non-filing for 12 months enables strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Gibraltar External Company Annual Return (if the Bermuda company maintains a place of business in Gibraltar)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the Gibraltar accounting reference period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 100 per day up to EUR 5,000; failure to file is a criminal offence and may lead to court-ordered deregistration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Bermuda exempted company is required to have an independent audit if it is a public company, licensed under the Banks and Trust Companies Act 1991, registered as an insurer, or subject to a Registrar audit order. Otherwise private exempted companies are exempt unless shareholders, lenders, or Gibraltar tax residence rules impose a higher threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; US GAAP is acceptable for private exempted companies by board resolution.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Companies (Beneficial Ownership) Regulations 2017, the exempted company must maintain a beneficial ownership register at the Bermuda registered office and file an annual confirmation with the Registrar on the anniversary of incorporation. Changes in beneficial ownership must be updated in the register and notified within 15 days.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Bermuda Exempted Company operates under a Tax-Exempt Zone classification. Bermuda levies no corporate income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax on qualifying exempted companies. Gibraltar imposes no corporate income tax on non-resident companies absent a permanent establishment. If central management and control is deemed to be exercised in Gibraltar, the Gibraltar standard headline rate is 12.5%, but this is fully mitigated by maintaining a Bermuda board, Bermuda economic substance, and no Gibraltar trading branch. Loss carryforward availability is 5 years in the event the entity inadvertently becomes a Gibraltar tax resident.
